agent_summary:
Authentication lane tested read-only against juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop v16/app v20.2.0, Express 4.22.1), ~120 requests within scope and rate limit.

Results by item:
- ATHN-01 (encrypted channel) DONE: no HTTPS listener (port 443 refused), no HSTS; credentials would travel over cleartext HTTP (x1).
- ATHN-02 (default creds) N/A: the default admin account admin@juice-sh.op demonstrably exists (security-question oracle), but confirming the password requires a POST /rest/user/login credential submission, not permitted read-only. Recorded a HIGH lead: /rest/memories (and /ftp/incident-support.kdbx) expose the admin password hash/tokens unauthenticated, enabling offline cracking/account takeover.
- ATHN-03 (lockout) N/A: measuring a lockout threshold needs repeated failed POST logins (brute force); observed only that the login form has no CAPTCHA.
- ATHN-04 (auth bypass) DONE: protected endpoints (/api/Users, /api/Users/1, /rest/basket/*, /api/Cards, /api/Addresss, /api/BasketItems, /b2b/v2/orders, /rest/order-history, authentication-details, SecurityAnswers) consistently return 401; whoami returns empty for anonymous and treats a forged/invalid JWT as anonymous; login OPTIONS does not reflect a hostile Origin. No no-credential bypass found, but /rest/memories leaks credential material (recorded).
- ATHN-05 (remember-password) DONE: "Remember me" feature present (i18n REMEMBER_ME) and the JWT is handled client-side (main.js authToken); full inspection of persisted-token flags needs an authenticated session (not available read-only).
- ATHN-06 (browser cache) DONE: sensitive API responses (e.g. /rest/admin/application-configuration) lack Cache-Control: no-store/Pragma: no-cache; SPA shell served cache-control: public.
- ATHN-07 (weak password policy) DONE + LOW lead: i18n shows complexity criteria are advisory (SHOW_PASSWORD_ADVICE) while only a length rule (INVALID_PASSWORD_LENGTH) is enforced; exact minimum was redacted by the gateway.
- ATHN-08 (weak security Q/A) DONE: /api/SecurityQuestions lists 14 weak guessable questions; /rest/user/security-question?email= is an unauthenticated enumeration oracle (valid accounts admin, jim, bender, support, ciso, morty, accountant, stan, wurstbrot, demo, emma, john, amy, J12934, bjoern@owasp.org return a question; unknown/empty return {}).
- ATHN-09 (weak change/reset) DONE + MEDIUM lead: change-password is a GET /rest/user/change-password?current=… (action+new password in query string, CSRF-prone) and reset relies on the weak enumerable security question; change/reset endpoints intentionally not exercised (writes).
- ATHN-10 (alt channels) DONE: B2B (/b2b/v2/orders) and REST basket require auth; Google OAuth is configured; no weaker unauthenticated channel found (admin-named application-version only leaks the public version).

Cross-lane observations re-confirmed for context (already owned by other lanes): /ftp null-byte extension bypass (package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, coupons, suspicious_errors.yml, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc all served via %2500.md), /support/logs and /ftp and /ftp/quarantine and /encryptionkeys directory listings, unauthenticated /metrics, /redirect allowlist-substring open redirect, and verbose Express stack traces (/profile, /dataerasure, /rest/country-mapping).

Left open: none fully blocked except the two POST-dependent items (02, 03) marked N/A with reasons. No writes proposed (lane is read-only).

leads.title: [agent] Admin password hash retrievable unauthenticated via /rest/memories enables offline credential recovery

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/memories with no session returns the embedded User object for the default admin account (id 4, username bkimminich, role admin) including its password hash, email and token fields. Combined with the fact that the login endpoints enforce credentials, this is the practical authentication weakness for this lane: an anonymous attacker can harvest the admin (and deluxe users') password hashes and crack them offline to achieve account takeover. Also reachable: the KeePass credential store /ftp/incident-support.kdbx (downloadable unauthenticated). Credential submission to confirm takeover was not performed (read-only lane).

leads.title: [agent] Password change implemented as GET /rest/user/change-password with secrets in query string

detail.text: main.js (GET http://juice.lab.test/main.js) references the password-change endpoint as GET /rest/user/change-password?current=…&new=…&repeat=…, placing the action and new password in a URL query string. This is the classic Juice Shop weakness: change via GET is CSRF-prone and leaks the new password into logs/history/referrer. The endpoint was intentionally NOT requested to avoid triggering a state change; flagged for the write-capable/authenticated review. Reset relies on weak, unauthenticated-enumerable security questions (/rest/user/security-question, /api/SecurityQuestions all generic knowledge questions).

leads.title: [agent] Weak password policy: complexity only advisory, minimum-length-only enforcement

detail.text: GET /assets/i18n/en.json shows the password complexity criteria (lower/upper/digit/special/min-chars) are rendered only as an advisory strength meter (SHOW_PASSWORD_ADVICE), while the only enforced validation is a length check (INVALID_PASSWORD_LENGTH). No complexity requirement is enforced on registration. Exact minimum length string was redacted by the gateway, but the structure confirms complexity is optional. A password-setting POST would confirm the minimum; flagged for the write-capable review.

evidence.summary: [agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ -> 200. Requested the app over both schemes: http://juice.lab.test/ returns 200 (served via nginx) while https://juice.lab.test:443 refused the connection outright. No HTTPS listener exists and no Strict-Transport-Security header is present, so login credentials would be submitted over cleartext HTTP.
